libs.note: This repository's source at the run's commit, not the published package of that version.

notes.text: A strict or identity parse of valid input returns the input itself, where Valibot and Zod return a copy.
Its guard, `is`, runs the parser, which copies what it reads, and drops the copy.
Classic `zod` generates a parser for each object schema on its first parse where the environment allows eval.
Its guard, `z.validate`, runs the parser where a schema has no compiled path, which copies what it reads, and drops the copy.

libs.label: Zod compiled
libs.note: Zod with each root through `z.compile`, its ahead-of-time mode.

notes.text: Each root through `z.compile`, which generates its parser and its validator ahead of time. A root it hands back uncompiled has no timed figure.
Each root through `z.compile`, which hands an invalid input to Zod's regular parser. A root it hands back uncompiled has no timed figure.
It carries the compiler `z.compile` needs, and compiles while the schema is built.
Its objects never compile: `zod/mini` has no generated parser.
Its guard, `z.validate`, runs the parser where a schema has no compiled path, which copies what it reads, and drops the copy.
Every row is a `Check` of its compiled validator, which stops at the first failure and builds no issues and no output.
A parse that drops keys deep-clones its input before it runs.
It keeps one schema of a definition and hands it back when the same definition is built again, which a figure marked `†` is of.
